analysis: Analysis 5: audit of Rule 3's dose predicate and its cost to the G134 stratum

inputs.documented_predicate_source: accord/dictionaries.py::dose_pct_diff and accord/phase3_mining.py::mine_rule3 (read by static parse)

documented_predicate.rule_3_description: Dosage Conflict: same drug, dose differs by more than 20 percent

over_min.formula: (max - min) / min * 100, equivalently max/min - 1, unbounded above

formula_fit_replication_note: The HF table is the one the annotated gold set was sampled from, and the /min denominator reproduces every one of its Rule 3 rows uniquely. The AKI table, a separate later cohort run, is reproduced uniquely by a DIFFERENT denominator, the nursing-side dose. Two output files of the same named rule carrying two different denominators is what an edited, unversioned mining implementation looks like, and it is a further reason the annotated table's predicate cannot be recovered from this repository. The sepsis table has too few rows to identify a formula.

unit_comparability_evidence.note: The annotated candidates table stores nursing_dose and discharge_dose as bare floats with no unit column, so unit comparability cannot have been enforced by anything downstream of mining. Units are recovered here from the deployed mentions table's dose strings.

cost_to_G134.why_it_matters: Rule 3 supplies 79 of the 134 pairs in G134, the stratum the thesis uses as its defect-free comparison arm on the assumption that Rules 3 and 4 exemplar correctness holds. A predicate defect in Rule 3 would remove that arm's interpretation.

membership.question: How many Rule 3 gold pairs would not exist under the documented predicate?
membership.equivalent_threshold: A stored value above 20 under the /min denominator is a ratio above 1.2, which is 16.67 percent under the documented /max denominator. The deployed rule is therefore slightly MORE permissive than documented, admitting pairs between 16.67 and 20 percent on the documented scale.

exemplar_selection.question: Can the denominator have changed WHICH dose pair was displayed?
exemplar_selection.why: mine_rule3 selects the (nursing, discharge) dose pair with the largest percent difference. (max - min) / min is max/min - 1 and (max - min) / max is 1 - min/max; both are strictly increasing functions of the ratio max/min, so they induce the same ordering over candidate dose pairs and the same argmax. The denominator affects the reported magnitude only, never the selection.
exemplar_selection.how_verified: The two formulas were evaluated on every observed dose pair and their induced rank orders compared elementwise. Identical rank order means the argmax, which is what mine_rule3 selects, is the same under either denominator.

verdict.the_stored_column_is: (max - min) / min * 100, equivalently max/min - 1, unbounded above
verdict.evidence_for_the_denominator: One candidate formula reproduces the stored value exactly on every Rule 3 gold pair and on every Rule 3 row of the full HF candidate table the gold set was drawn from. The documented formula reproduces none of them, and provably cannot, since it is bounded in [0, 100) and most stored values exceed 100.
verdict.evidence_against_incomparable_quantities: Among the Rule 3 gold pairs whose admission and drug key has any unit-bearing mention in the deployed mentions table, almost none use more than one unit, and of the pairs whose two stored dose values can be matched back to a unit-bearing mention, none compares two different units. The unit vocabulary is dominated by a single mass unit. A bolus against a maintenance rate would show as two different units or as a multi-unit key, and it does not.
verdict.where_the_offending_implementation_is: Not in this repository. The only definition of the percent difference in the tree uses the documented max denominator and is asserted bounded in its own docstring, so no code under version control can produce the stored values. The implementation that produced the annotated candidates table is the original mining notebook, which is not on disk.
verdict.does_G134_survive: As a SET, yes: only one of the 79 Rule 3 gold pairs would fail the documented threshold, and the denominator cannot have changed which dose pair was displayed, so Rule 3's exemplar-correctness credit of 1.0 is not overturned by this finding. As a set of REPORTED QUANTITIES, no: the stored dose_diff_pct is not the documented quantity, most of its values are impossible under the stated definition, and the threshold actually applied is 16.67 percent on the documented scale rather than 20.
verdict.what_should_change_in_the_thesis: State the predicate that was actually applied, or recompute the column with the documented predicate and drop the one pair that then fails the threshold. Either way the Rule 3 exemplar-correctness credit of 1.0 in results/accord/exemplar_direct/exemplar_direct.json rests on a predicate whose implementation is absent from the repository, so it is unverified rather than verified.

data_agreement: Counts, proportions, formula names and unit names only. Dose values were read in process to test arithmetic identities and none is written. No clinical note text and no patient or admission identifier appears in this artifact; asserted in code before writing.
